parsed.summary: The change makes negative percents give no discount and the added tests for -5 pass on Checkout and Order Import. However, the diff also silently removed the upper bound, so percents over 100 now produce negative totals, and nothing in the requirement asked for that.

findings.title: Percent above 100 no longer rejected; yields negative totals
findings.detail: The original range check threw for percent < 0 or > 100. REQ-21 only asks to change the negative case. The diff removed the whole check and only floors at 0, so percent > 100 now gives discountCents > subtotal and a negative total (e.g. 200 cents at 150% gives -100). The new test at tests/checkout.test.ts:15 only asserts that checkout does not throw at 150, so it locks in the changed behaviour without checking the total. Both Checkout and Order Import reach this code, so a bad promo value or partner row can now produce a negative charge instead of an error. The author's brief says 'a bad promo percent no longer fails checkout', which goes beyond the requirement.
findings.suggestedCheck: Restore the upper-bound RangeError for percent > 100 (only floor negatives), and add a test that 150% still throws in both Checkout and Order Import.

findings.title: Order Import preservation for 0 to 100 percents is not tested
findings.detail: REQ-21 says percents from 0 to 100 keep their totals, and Order Import is an affected workflow. The only passing import tests cover the wrong column count and -5. The 0 to 100 preservation test at tests/checkout.test.ts:20 reaches only checkoutTotal. No passing test shows Order Import totals for percents in 0..100 are unchanged. The shared code path makes this likely fine, but it is not established by a test.
findings.suggestedCheck: Add an importOrder test, e.g. 'A-3,200,10' totals 180 and 'A-4,200,100' totals 0, and run it.

findings.title: Callers claim not verified; other callers may depend on the old throw
findings.detail: The author claims applyDiscount() has no callers other than Checkout and Order Import. The code index lists only those two, but the index is not proof, and tests/ledger.test.ts / src/payments/ledger.ts were not shown to be unaffected. Any caller that relied on the RangeError for validation now gets a silent result.
findings.suggestedCheck: Search the whole repo (including non-indexed and dynamic uses) for applyDiscount references and confirm none relied on the throw.

couldNotDecide.question: Whether operations or product intend percents above 100 to be rejected, clamped to 100, or accepted.
couldNotDecide.checkThatWouldHelp: Ask the requirement owner; the requirement is silent on values over 100 and the base version rejected them.
